title: Provisioning credit runway and operator approval playbook for burstable Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Define an operational playbook and API/console flows that let customers request Dedicated capacity with a mix of committed throughput and burstable credit runway, and let operators approve or auto-approve requests based on risk signals. This ticket scopes the provisioning lifecycle for burstable reservations, SLO enforcement at reservation boundaries, and the approval matrix for operator override.

Why now: customers are asking for a lower-friction path between ad-hoc bursts and full committed reservations. We need a safe way to let customers temporarily exceed committed throughput using a credit runway while protecting other tenants and preserving SLA guarantees.

Scope (what this ticket will deliver):
- Product spec for a two-part reservation model: (1) committed baseline throughput, (2) burst credits with configurable runway (hours/days).
- Approval matrix: auto-approve thresholds (low-risk accounts, <$5k/month, single-region) and an operator approval flow for higher-risk requests with explicit guardrails.
- Console UX: request form with suggested baseline, burst runway slider, risk score and estimated cost delta; operator review queue with quick actions and justification fields.
- API endpoints for submitting, amending, and cancelling runway requests; webhooks for approval status changes.
- Observable signals and SLO enforcement: per-reservation throttles, soft-fallback to compatible model variants, and notifications for near-credit exhaustion.
- Playbook docs for support/operators: triage steps, rollback actions, escalation contacts, and cost reconciliation checklist.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Granularity of commitments: hourly vs daily vs monthly. We recommend daily minimums for billing simplicity but allow hourly runway for short bursts; this balances accuracy vs invoicing complexity.
- Auto-approve aggressiveness: tighter thresholds reduce misuse but increase operator load; we propose conservative defaults that can be tuned per customer tier.
- Isolation model: hard isolation (dedicated nodes pinned) vs soft isolation (logical shaping). Hard isolation is safer but raises unit cost; the playbook includes recommended isolation levels per risk band.

Decisions made so far:
- Use a credit-based runway charged at a burst multiplier (e.g., 1.4x committed token rate) rather than raw on-demand pricing, to encourage sensible usage while covering cost delta.
- Auto-approve thresholds: auto for customers with <30 days usage, less than $5k committed monthly, and risk score < 0.25. Others route to ops queue.
- Observability: add per-reservation quota dashboards to Console and emit a "runway_exhaustion" event to customers and internal alerts.

Artifacts and links: PRD (Confluence) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/credit-runway-prd; Wireframes (Figma) - https://figma.redwood.ai/provisioning/burst-runway; Spike notes (Drive) - https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1xRunwaySpike; Backend spike PR - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4217; Ops runbook draft - https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/dedicated-runbook-draft.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal review required for billing language (billing and refunds for partial-day credits) - assigned to Priya Kapoor in Legal.
- Kernel/runtime integration: need ENG-18234 to land the per-reservation throttling hooks for safe soft-fallback.
- Pricing model approval from Finance for the burst multiplier.

Next steps (owner: Liam Chen):
- Finalize PRD and edge-case billing examples by 2025-02-18.
- Deliver Console request form wireframes and hand off to Design for Accessibility pass by 2025-02-21.
- Kick off API design RFC and sequence diagram; link to ENG spike PR and assign backend owners.
- Prepare support/operator playbook and tabletop run-through with SRE and Support on 2025-02-25.

Acceptance criteria:
- PRD approved by PM, Eng lead, Finance, and Legal.
- Console prototype with runway slider and risk score visible in staging.
- API spec and webhook contract merged into the api-spec repo.
- Ops runbook published with triage steps, rollback commands, and escalation contacts.
- Unit and integration tests covering per-reservation quota enforcement and runway depletion behavior.

Why this is different from typical reservations: it provides a middle ground between ad-hoc bursts and long-term commitments, designed to reduce friction for customers while maintaining predictable economics for Redwood and minimizing cross-tenant risk.
